Trust decision: the browser trusts every property reachable on the server-sent `effects` object (and evals `js`/`xjs`/`scripts` from it) while the query-string parser writes attacker-chosen dotted keys into plain nested containers; the fix hardens 14 effect/commit sites plus the parser — `pattern_fit: A+B`.

Strongest lever: the root cause sits in a vendored Alpine plugin (`js/plugins/history/index.js:255-303`) two directories from the effect handlers a summary-only reader lands on, and the pinned commit already had a *partial* defence (`Object.create(null)` at line 280) that did not work.

Biggest red flag: none of the listed flags hold; the practical cost is that testing needs `npm run build` (no `dist/` in the pinned tree) plus headless-Chrome Dusk suites, and repo size could not be measured.
